annotations.title: What's under the street at an address

description: Looks up what public records say is under the street in front of one street address in New York City, Washington, DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, and Dallas. Returns each utility likely in the street (water, sewer, storm drain, gas, electric, telecom, steam) with its distance from the lot line, its expected depth and the code or standard behind it, and how the line was placed (the owner's published map, excavation permits on the block, or inferred) with a confidence label; the water service line's lead status where the city publishes it by address; the house sewer; digging permitted there today; the newest permits out front, each with its street, its distance from the address and its issue date (or its start date, marked scheduled when the work hasn't begun), and whether it is one of several permits for the same long-running job; and the nearest hydrant, catch basin and manhole. Use it for site research, scoping an excavation, or due diligence on a property: what is under the street or sidewalk at an address, whether planned digging might meet a line, and whether the service line is lead. Answers are public-records evidence with a records-as-of date, not a survey or a utility locate, and end with the city's 811 notice. An address outside these cities, or with no exact match, returns an error saying what was found instead.

address.description: A street address with house number, in New York City, Washington, DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, or Dallas. Include the city, e.g. "200 N Spring St, Los Angeles" or "33 Union Square West, Manhattan".

city.description: Which city the address is in, to search only that city and rule out a lookalike address elsewhere. One of "nyc" for New York City, "dc" for Washington, DC, "sf" for San Francisco, "la" for Los Angeles, "sd" for San Diego, "sea" for Seattle, "den" for Denver, "chi" for Chicago, "dal" for Dallas. The full name or a common short form works too, in any case: "Los Angeles", "NYC", "Brooklyn", "D.C.".

name: whats_under

address.description: The address as the city geocoder found it

credits.description: The credit the city's publishers ask for, and OpenStreetMap's; quote it with the records

fartherLines.description: Only when no line is within reach of the lot line: the nearest lines farther out, up to about 400 ft

incomplete.description: Some map data failed to load; the answer may miss records

published.description: Whether the city publishes service line material by lot

matchDiffers.description: Whether the matched address reads differently from the one asked for

matchedAddress.description: The address the answer is for; the same as address, kept beside requestedAddress

anyOf.description: Meters from the address to the nearest block the permit is filed on

issued.description: The day the city issued the permit; null where the city publishes no issue date (Los Angeles, Denver), so go by workStart

nth.description: This permit's place in the job, 1 for the first

permits.description: Permits filed for this one job

renewals.description: Permits the city itself filed as a renewal or extension (New York only); null where the city does not say

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the job's first work start

through.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the job's last work end

workOrder.description: The utility's work order, where the permit names one

job.description: Set when this permit is one of 3 or more for the same job, re-permitted as the work dragged on (same holder and work order, or same holder, work and street, each following closely)

recordsAsOf.description: When the records were last built, ISO 8601

requestedAddress.description: The address as it was asked for

basis.description: Where the depth comes from: federal or state code, city standard

measuredFt.description: Depth from the owner’s records, where published

distanceFromLotLineFt.description: To the line as drawn on the map, not surveyed
